understanding: List every employee with their direct manager's name; employees with no manager must still appear with blank manager.
edge_cases: two employees report to the same manager
expected: 4 rows: Andrew Adams/NULL, Nancy Edwards/Andrew Adams, Jane Peacock/Nancy Edwards, Margaret Park/Nancy Edwards
got: 3 rows; Andrew Adams (no manager) is missing
reason: INNER JOIN drops employees with no manager (the general manager); a LEFT JOIN was required.

understanding: Count customers per employee via SupportRepId, listing all employees including those with 0.
edge_cases: employee with no customers (2 of them)
expected: Jane Peacock 2, Nancy Edwards 1, Andrew Adams 0, Margaret Park 0
reason: LEFT JOIN with COUNT(c.CustomerId) yields 0 for employees without customers and ignores NULL support rep.

understanding: Count albums whose total duration exceeds 1 hour (3,600,000 ms) and that have at least one track with empty/NULL Composer.
edge_cases: album exactly 3,600,000 ms with NULL composer (excluded)
long album with all composers filled
reason: Strict > on the summed milliseconds and EXISTS on NULL/empty composer match the expected result including boundary cases.

understanding: 2023 invoice revenue per support employee through the customers they support, with employee name and revenue.
edge_cases: employee whose customer has only non-2023 invoices
expected: Andrew Adams 0, Nancy Edwards 16.5, Jane Peacock 0
got: Andrew Adams 0.0, Nancy Edwards 16.5, Jane Peacock 0.0
reason: Year filter is in the LEFT JOIN condition, so employees with no 2023 revenue are kept with 0 and boundaries are correct.

understanding: For each media type, count distinct tracks sold at least once.
edge_cases: media type with no sold tracks (M3)
reason: COUNT(DISTINCT) avoids double-counting repeated sales; media types with zero sold tracks are omitted, which is acceptable under a reasonable reading but a risk if the reference expects 0 rows.

understanding: Count customers who bought at least one Rock track and at least one Jazz track (possibly in different invoices).
edge_cases: customer with only Rock bought twice
customer with Rock+Jazz in same invoice
customer with Rock and Jazz in different invoices
reason: Grouping by customer with COUNT(DISTINCT genre name)=2 correctly handles multiple invoices and repeated lines.

understanding: Sum of invoice totals for 2025-01-01 through 2025-03-31 inclusive.
reason: Half-open range with < '2025-04-01' correctly includes the last day with time component.

understanding: Monthly revenue for 2025 ordered by month ascending.
reason: Year filter, month grouping, zero-padded month ordering and rounding are all right; months without sales are omitted, which is the natural reading.

understanding: Percent change in total revenue from 2024 to 2025, rounded to 2 decimals.
edge_cases: other years (2023, 2026) with large totals excluded
reason: Conditional sums per year and the percent formula match; excludes other years. Division by zero only if no 2024 data, unlikely.

understanding: Count distinct tracks across all playlists named 'Music' (several playlists may share the name).
edge_cases: track present in both Music playlists (10)
track in Music and in other playlist
reason: JOIN on all Music playlists with COUNT(DISTINCT TrackId) dedupes tracks shared across duplicate-named playlists.
